title: "Can't do it today" is a slip, not a pause
origin: Spec #12 (commands and safety), Should: a "can't do it today" text gets the slip treatment, not a pause

history.text: Plan's yours, Jordan. I'll hold you to it. You in?
LET'S GO. Day 1 was Saturday, keep it rolling 🏃

plan.reason: Running every day builds the habit fast.

testerLines: can't do it today, need a break, slammed at work
whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: a skipped day mustn't be read as a request to pause.
shouldHaveHappened: After the morning kickoff, "can't do it today" is treated as a slip: ZOH holds the line once, warmly and without guilt (the full run, maybe later today) or offers a smaller version. It doesn't offer, suggest or confirm pausing its texts, and doesn't ask why they want a break as if they'd asked to pause.
